+                # Re-collection (handle_dupes=False) creates fresh child nodes.
+                # Reuse previously-seen Directory children so that fixture
+                # registration (keyed by node identity) remains valid. (#14635)
+                #
+                # This post-processing reconciliation is intentional: the
+                # collection architecture is not ready for a session-global
+                # Directory node registry, and pushing deduplication into
+                # individual collectors (Dir.collect / Package.collect) would
+                # leak session-level concerns into node code and miss
+                # third-party Directory subclasses.
+                prev_result = self._collection_cache[node].result
+                prev_dirs = {
+                    child.path: child
+                    for child in prev_result
+                    if isinstance(child, nodes.Directory)
+                }
+                if prev_dirs:
+                    rep.result = [
+                        prev_dirs.get(child.path, child)
+                        if isinstance(child, nodes.Directory)
+                        else child
+                        for child in rep.result
+                    ]

problem_statement:
Error collecting tests on 9.1.1 - fixtures not found when a parent directory appears multiple times in a argument list 

_Disclosure: I have used AI to investigate this issue but am able to reproduce everything locally._

In Home Assistant, we tried to upgrade from PyTest 9.0.3 to 9.1.1 in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/174371 (some diagnosis in comments)

We first ran into a collection abort issue in 9.1.0 that got fixed in 9.1.1 with https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14591.

With 9.1.1 we're hitting a new issue when collecting tests.

```
――――――――――――――― ERROR collecting tests/components/tts/test_init.py ―――――――――――――――
In tests/components/tts/test_init.py::test_setup_component_no_access_cache_folder: function uses no argument 'init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect'
```

I / Claude were not able to get a reproduction going outside of HA, so to reproduce you need to set up a HA dev env.

Step 1: Get a Home Assistant dev environment.

```
gh repo clone home-assistant/core
cd core
script/setup
```

```
> uv pip freeze | grep pytest
pytest==9.0.3
...
```

Step 2: Test collection passes

```
pytest --collect-only \
  tests/components/water_heater \
  tests/test_config_entries.py \
  tests/components/tts/test_init.py
```

Step 3: upgrade to pytest 9.1.1

```
uv pip install pytest==9.1.1
```

Step 4: Test collection fails

```
❯ uv pip install pytest==9.1.1
Resolved 5 packages in 97ms
Uninstalled 1 package in 15ms
Installed 1 package in 9ms
 - pytest==9.0.3
 + pytest==9.1.1
❯ pytest --collect-only \
  tests/components/water_heater \
  tests/test_config_entries.py \
  tests/components/tts/test_init.py
Test session starts (platform: darwin, Python 3.14.5, pytest 9.1.1, pytest-sugar 1.1.1)
rootdir: /Users/paulus/dev/hass/core
configfile: pyproject.toml
plugins: syrupy-5.3.2, pytest_freezer-0.4.9, socket-0.8.0, unordered-0.7.0, cov-7.1.0, xdist-3.8.0, typeguard-4.5.2, timeout-2.4.0, asyncio-1.4.0, github-actions-annotate-failures-0.4.0, aiohttp-1.1.1, sugar-1.1.1, rerunfailures-16.0.1, respx-0.23.1, picked-0.5.1, requests-mock-1.12.1, anyio-4.13.0
asyncio: mode=Mode.AUTO, debug=True, asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope=function, asyncio_default_test_loop_scope=function
collecting 3564 items                                                            
――――――――――――――― ERROR collecting tests/components/tts/test_init.py ―――――――――――――――
In tests/components/tts/test_init.py::test_setup_component_no_access_cache_folder: function uses no argument 'init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect'
collected 3564 items / 1 error  
```

Expand below to get a more elaborate AI generated description of the issue

<details>
<summary>AI generated diagnosis</summary>

### Description

In pytest 9.1 (both 9.1.0 and 9.1.1), the computed fixture closure of a test can change depending on **which unrelated paths were collected before it**. When a test relies on *implicit indirect* parametrization — `@pytest.mark.parametrize("some_fixture", [...])` where the test depends on `some_fixture` only transitively, not as a direct argument — collecting certain unrelated directories first causes that fixture to drop out of the closure, and collection fails with:

```
function uses no argument 'some_fixture'
```

The same test collects fine when run on its own, or when the other paths are collected in a different order. This passes on 9.0.3 and fails on 9.1.x, so it's a regression. I believe it is related to the fixture override-precedence rework (#14513 / PR #14566), which changed override ordering from registration-order to visibility/scope-order.

A test's fixture closure should be independent of what unrelated paths were collected earlier in the session.

### Reproduction

This reproduces against the public Home Assistant repo (the fixture graph that triggers it is non-trivial; I have not yet reduced it to a standalone `conftest.py`, but the repro below is fully deterministic and takes three commands):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/home-assistant/core hass-core
cd hass-core
git checkout 957c24fcd724          # any recent dev commit works
python -m venv venv && . venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements_test.txt -r requirements.txt   # or: pip install -e . pytest-aiohttp syrupy ...
pip install pytest==9.1.1

# Order matters. This fails:
pytest --collect-only \
  tests/components/water_heater \
  tests/test_config_entries.py \
  tests/components/tts/test_init.py
```

**Actual (9.1.1):**

```
ERROR collecting tests/components/tts/test_init.py
In tests/components/tts/test_init.py::test_setup_component_no_access_cache_folder: function uses no argument 'init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect'
!!! Interrupted: 1 error during collection !!!
```

**Expected (and actual on 9.0.3):** clean collection, ~3.6k tests collected, no error.

Notes on determinism:
- Deterministic across `PYTHONHASHSEED` (fails on random seeds and on fixed seeds 0–5).
- The failing file passes in isolation: `pytest --collect-only tests/components/tts/test_init.py` ✅.
- Reversing the order (e.g. collecting `tts` first) also passes — it is purely the order in which the earlier paths are collected.
- `--collect-only` is enough; no xdist required (we originally hit it under `-n auto --dist=loadfile`, but it's not xdist-specific).

### Why the test is structured this way (for context)

`tests/components/tts/test_init.py::test_setup_component_no_access_cache_folder`:

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect", [OSError(2, "No access")])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("setup", ["mock_setup", "mock_config_entry_setup"], indirect=True)
async def test_setup_component_no_access_cache_folder(
    hass, mock_tts_init_cache_dir, setup
):
    ...
```

The closure that makes the `init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect` parametrize valid:

- the test directly requests `mock_tts_init_cache_dir` (in `tests/components/conftest.py`)
- `mock_tts_init_cache_dir` → requests `init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect` (also `tests/components/conftest.py`)
- additionally, `tests/components/tts/conftest.py` has an **autouse fixture that overrides a parent fixture and requests the same-named super**:
  ```python
  @pytest.fixture(autouse=True, name="mock_tts_cache_dir")
  def mock_tts_cache_dir_fixture_autouse(mock_tts_cache_dir):  # requests the parent of the same name
      return mock_tts_cache_dir
  ```
  whose parent (`tests/components/conftest.py`) transitively also reaches `init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect`.

Under 9.1 with a triggering prefix, `init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect` is no longer present in the closure, even though `mock_tts_init_cache_dir` is still requested directly — which is what makes this look like a closure-computation bug tied to the new override ordering rather than intended behavior.

### Environment

- pytest 9.1.1 (also reproduces on 9.1.0); **last known good: 9.0.3**
- pluggy 1.6.0
- Python 3.14.5
- macOS (Darwin arm64); also seen on Linux CI (Python 3.14.5)

### Suspected cause

#14513 / PR #14566 — fixture override ordering changed from registration-order to visibility-order. The order-dependence of the closure is the smell: with the new ordering, resolving an overridden fixture for the tts test appears to pick a fixturedef that no longer carries the `init_tts_cache_dir_side_effect` dependency, depending on what was registered while collecting earlier paths.

### Related

- #14591 — separate 9.1.0 regression ("duplicate parametrization of '<arg>'" when a fixture has `params=` and a test re-parametrizes it with `indirect=True`), fixed in 9.1.1. This report is a *different* problem that 9.1.1 does not fix.

</details>

from sklearn.neighbors import KDTree

problem_statement:
Using `move_to` on a numpy array with negative stride crashes the Python process

The `move_to` function we have for moving arrays from one namespace to another can crash the Python process when you ask it to move an array with negative strides. I found this while working on `PCA` where we have an array with negative stride (`Vt` from `_fit_truncated`).

The code below is a reproducer:

```python
import numpy as np
import torch
import sklearn
from sklearn.utils._array_api import get_namespace_and_device, move_to

def make_negative_strided():
    """A small, contiguous-source array viewed with a negative stride."""
    a = np.arange(12.0).reshape(3, 4)[:, ::-1]
    assert not a.flags["C_CONTIGUOUS"]
    assert a.strides[-1] < 0
    return a

a = make_negative_strided()
with sklearn.config_context(array_api_dispatch=True):
    xp, _, device = get_namespace_and_device(torch.asarray([1.0]))
    try:
        move_to(a, xp=xp, device=device)
    except Exception as exc:  # it is not caught
        print("Caught a Python exception (unexpected):", type(exc).__name__, exc)
    else:
        # this doesn't happen
        print("move_to returned without error (unexpected)")

    # instead the process exits with a SIGABRT
```

AI tells me that a possible fix is to call `np.ascontiguousarray(array)` if the input `array` is an array with negative stride. In addition we should [only apply this workaround in the case where the `move_to` target is torch](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/34307#issuecomment-4778962780). The comment for the workaround should also include a link to https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/188023 and this issue so we can know when the work around can be removed.

Something like this, but with a check for torch as target:
```diff
--- a/sklearn/utils/_array_api.py
+++ b/sklearn/utils/_array_api.py
@@ def move_to(*arrays, xp, device):
             xp_array, _, device_array = get_namespace_and_device(array)
             if xp == xp_array and device == device_array:
                 converted_arrays.append(array)
             else:
+                strides = getattr(array, "strides", None)
+                if strides is not None and any(
+                    stride < 0 for stride in strides
+                ):
+                    # Some libraries (e.g. torch) do not raise a catchable
+                    # Python exception but abort the whole process when a NumPy
+                    # array with negative or zero strides is imported via DLPack
+                    # (such arrays are produced for instance by ``a[::-1]``
+                    # reversals, as done by ARPACK). The ``except`` clause below
+                    # therefore cannot protect against it, so the source array is
+                    # made contiguous first to guarantee positive strides.
+                    array = numpy.ascontiguousarray(array)
                 try:
                     # The dlpack protocol is the future proof and library agnostic
                     # method to transfer arrays across namespace and device boundaries
                     # hence this method is attempted first and going through NumPy is
                     # only used as fallback in case of failure.
                     # Note: copy=None is the default since array-api 2023.12. Namespace
                     # libraries should only trigger a copy automatically if needed.
                     array_converted = xp.from_dlpack(array, device=device)
```

What do others think about this? I am also wondering if this is a bug in numpy's DLPack implementation (should not expose arrays with negative stride) or if this is a bug in torch (should check for negative stride before doing anything)?

I think that `numpy.ascontiguousarray(array)` is free for most arrays, those that already full fill it. For arrays that are not already contiguous I don't know what the cost is, but I think there is no alternative?

problem_statement:
hermes update (Windows) stops the dashboard server but only restarts the gateway — web UI chat left dead until manual relaunch

## Environment
- hermes-agent 0.18.0, checkout at 7203898ce
- Windows 11 Home (10.0.26200), Python 3.11.15
- Standalone web dashboard started with `hermes dashboard` (default port 9119), used from Chrome

## Symptom
After running `hermes update`, the web dashboard's chat never reconnects. The update output shows the asymmetry:

```
→ Stopping Windows gateway process(es) before updating Hermes...
  ✓ Paused gateway profile(s): default
...
✓ Update complete!
  ✓ Restarting Windows gateway profile(s): default
```

The pre-update stop takes down the dashboard server along with the gateway, but the post-update resume only restarts the gateway profile. Nothing listens on 9119 afterward, so any open dashboard tab shows a dead chat connection with no hint that the server is gone. The user-visible failure is "chat not connecting" — it looks like a gateway or network problem, not a missing process.

## Related: `hermes dashboard --status` reports false positives
While diagnosing, `hermes dashboard --status` claimed dashboards were running when none was listening:

```
3 hermes dashboard process(es) running:
    PID 16488
    PID 25324
    PID 31924
```

- 16488 / 25324 were the **desktop app's** internal `serve --port 0` backend (IPC-gated, not a usable dashboard)
- 31924 no longer existed at all

So the natural post-update health check also lies, which makes the missing-dashboard state harder to spot.

## Suggested fix
Track the dashboard server the same way gateway profiles are tracked, and either restart it in the post-update resume step or print an explicit "dashboard was stopped — run `hermes dashboard` to restore the web UI" notice. Separately, `--status` should verify the recorded PIDs are alive and actually bound to a listening port before reporting them as running.

problem_statement:
DEFAULT_CONFIG declares "kanban" twice; the auto_subscribe_on_create default is silently dropped

### What happens

`DEFAULT_CONFIG` declares the `"kanban"` key twice, so the first block is silently dropped and the `auto_subscribe_on_create` default is missing from `DEFAULT_CONFIG`.

```python
from hermes_cli.config import DEFAULT_CONFIG
"auto_subscribe_on_create" in DEFAULT_CONFIG["kanban"]   # -> False
```

### Where

`hermes_cli/config.py`, `DEFAULT_CONFIG`:

- First block: `"kanban": {"auto_subscribe_on_create": True}`
- Later block: `"kanban": {"dispatch_in_gateway": True, "dispatch_interval_seconds": 60, ...}`

Python keeps only the last literal for a duplicate key, so the first block (and its `auto_subscribe_on_create` default) is discarded.

### Impact

`tools/kanban_tools.py` reads the value with `cfg_get(cfg, "kanban", "auto_subscribe_on_create", default=True)`, so the hardcoded fallback masks the missing default at runtime today. But:
- The documented default is absent from `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, so config templates and `hermes config show` omit it.
- The duplicate key is a latent hazard: any future key added to the first block would also silently disappear.

### Expected

A single `kanban` block in `DEFAULT_CONFIG` that carries every documented default, including `auto_subscribe_on_create`.

A fix with regression tests is in #55778.

subscription

kimi-for-coding

### What issue are you seeing?

When using `kimi acp` mode, authentication **requires** running `kimi acp --login` interactively. Configuring credentials in `setting.toml` (e.g. API Key) has no effect — ACP mode does not read these settings and still demands a fresh login.

Since `kimi acp --login` requires manual interaction each time, it blocks use cases like background services, CI/CD pipelines, or any headless ACP integration.

problem_statement:
[Bug]: iOS Markdown list items truncate with ellipses when text wraps

# [Bug]: iOS Markdown list items truncate with ellipses when text wraps

## Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

In the official OpenClaw 2026.7.2 Apple app, completed assistant Markdown list items are truncated with an ellipsis instead of expanding vertically when their text wraps; the same stored response reproduces on both iPad and iPhone, while prose outside the list remains fully visible.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install OpenClaw 2026.7.2 on an iPad and an iPhone.
2. Open the same completed assistant response containing list items long enough to wrap. The response used for the attached evidence contained this Markdown:

   ```markdown
   - The selected account name is shown as the author of the public issue.
   - The issue is not posted by an official OpenClaw organization account or a separate assistant account.
   - You can create an issue in the public repository without being an OpenClaw organization member.
   - Use a personal GitHub account rather than a company account, because the company username may remain visible as the public author.
   - You do not need to share your password; GitHub authenticates in the browser and only grants the GitHub CLI access on the Mac.
   ```

   The actual observed response was in Korean and is visible in the attached screenshots.
3. View the completed response on iPad.
4. View the same stored response on iPhone without regenerating it.
5. Observe the list items that require more vertical space.

## Expected behavior

Every list item should wrap to as many lines as needed so the full stored message remains visible, with no ellipsis on either iPad or iPhone.

## Actual behavior

- On iPad, the attached response displays roughly one line per list item and truncates longer items with `…`.
- On iPhone, the same response displays roughly two lines per list item and truncates the remaining text with `…`.
- Prose immediately before and after the list displays in full on both devices.
- In another observed response, three shorter list items fit on iPad but truncated on iPhone, showing that which items fail changes with the available width.

## OpenClaw version

2026.7.2

## Operating system

- iPadOS 26.5.2 on iPad14,4 (iPad Pro 11-inch, 4th generation)
- iOS 26.5.2 on iPhone16,2 (iPhone 15 Pro Max)

## Install method

Official Apple app update

## Model

openai/gpt-5.6-sol. The issue is observed while rendering the same already-stored assistant response; no regeneration is involved.

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> OpenAI. The provider path is not expected to affect this reproduction because both devices render the same stored message payload.

## Additional provider/model setup details

No per-device model or provider difference. Both screenshots show the same completed response from the same OpenClaw session.

## Logs

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The linked comparison report was generated from two direct device screenshots of the same stored response:

1. iPad: list items are constrained to roughly one line and end in ellipses.
2. iPhone: the same message allows roughly two lines but still truncates longer items.

The report preserves the side-by-side visual evidence; the original local screenshots contain no account name, email address, gateway token, or private conversation title.

Supporting comparison report: https://www.lazyweb.com/report/lazyweb/e07849fc-637d-4270-b6e9-09ab991ca51b/?source=create

Width-dependent follow-up analysis: https://www.lazyweb.com/report/lazyweb/a548ebe8-e5b2-4233-af28-c81d726c09a5/?source=create

## Impact and severity

- Affected: Users reading completed Markdown list responses in the OpenClaw Apple app on iPad or iPhone.
- Severity: High for affected responses because part of the assistant's stored answer is hidden with no expansion control.
- Frequency: Reproduced on both tested devices with the same response; additional list responses also showed width-dependent truncation.
- Consequence: Instructions, qualifications, and other content after the visible line limit cannot be read in the app. This is especially disruptive for structured, long-form work on iPad.

## Additional information

- The first observed affected app version is 2026.7.2.
- Exact last-known-good behavior for native list wrapping: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. Version 2026.7.1 did not use the same native list presentation.
- Native Markdown list rendering was introduced by PR #111223: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111223
- The current list view uses a SwiftUI `Grid`/`GridRow` layout in `ChatMarkdownBlockViews.swift`. This is implementation context only; the screenshots and deterministic cross-device comparison are the evidence for the bug.
- A regression test should verify the measured/rendered height and full visibility of long multi-line list items, including Korean text, rather than only verifying that the view builds at a narrow width.

problem_statement:
fix(delegate_task): silent timeout kills subagents without notifying parent session

## Problem

`delegate_task` subagents that exceed the internal timeout (~5min) are silently killed. The `[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE]` message is never delivered to the parent session. The parent session has no way to know the task failed — it appears as if the task is still running, and the user/agent waits indefinitely for a result that will never arrive.

## Reproduction

1. Dispatch a `delegate_task` with a research-heavy goal (e.g. 6+ `web_search` calls + content analysis)
2. The subagent runs for >5 minutes
3. The subagent is killed silently (no error, no completion message)
4. The parent session never receives `[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE]`
5. The parent agent has no signal that the task failed — it may tell the user "the task is still running" or simply move on without reporting the failure

## Real-world impact

In a single session, 3+ research subagents were dispatched and all silently disappeared:
- Dark Factory orchestrator pattern research (6 web searches)
- Codex CLI token extraction research (web searches + terminal commands)
- Main-agent model choice research (5+ web searches)

Each ran for 6-10 minutes, exceeded the timeout, and was killed without any notification to the parent. The parent agent incorrectly reported "tasks are still running" to the user, who then asked "do they really still run?" — exposing the silent failure.

## Root cause

The `delegate_task` background execution has an internal timeout that kills long-running subagents. When the timeout fires:
1. The subagent process is terminated
2. No `[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE]` (or equivalent timeout/error message) is delivered to the parent session
3. The parent session's context has no record that the delegation was attempted, timed out, or failed

This is distinct from:
- #48864 (gateway restart loses in-flight delegations) — our issue happens WITHOUT a restart
- #35986 (Kanban stale detection) — our issue is about delegate_task specifically, not Kanban

## Proposed fix

Three options, not mutually exclusive:

### Option A: Deliver timeout notification (minimal fix)
When a subagent times out, deliver a message to the parent session:
```
[ASYNC DELEGATION TIMEOUT — deleg_XXXX]
A background delegation has exceeded the timeout and was terminated.
Goal: <goal summary>
Duration: <elapsed>s
Partial output (if any): <last N lines>
```
This ensures the parent agent can react (retry, inform user, try alternative approach).

### Option B: Configurable timeout
Make the delegate_task timeout configurable:
- `delegate_task(goal=..., timeout=600)` — per-task timeout in seconds
- Or env var: `HERMES_DELEGATE_TASK_TIMEOUT=600`
- Default stays at current value (~300s) for backward compat
- Research-heavy tasks (web search, multi-step analysis) can opt into longer timeouts

### Option C: Heartbeat / progress signal
For long-running subagents, deliver periodic progress signals to the parent:
```
[ASYNC DELEGATION PROGRESS — deleg_XXXX]
Still running... 3/6 web searches completed, 180s elapsed
```
This gives the parent visibility without waiting for completion.

## Recommendation

**Option A + B together** would solve the immediate problem:
- A ensures no silent failure (the parent ALWAYS gets a message — success, error, or timeout)
- B allows research-heavy tasks to run longer without being killed

Option C is a nice-to-have for UX but not essential.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (by Nous Research)
- macOS 26.4.1
- Model: z-ai/glm-5.2 via OpenRouter
- delegate_task used extensively for cross-LLM research and validation tasks

problem_statement:
Feature: expose tool_call_history in subagent_stop hook payload

## Problem

The `subagent_stop` shell hook currently receives:
- `child_summary` (self-reported narrative text)
- `child_status`, `child_role`, `child_task`, `duration_ms`

It does **not** include the child agent's actual `tool_call_history` — the list of tool invocations the subagent made. This means:

1. **Narrative Override attacks** cannot be definitively detected. A subagent can claim "wrote report.json" in its summary but actually have written to a different file, or performed undisclosed operations.
2. **Governance layers cannot validate** assertions in child_summary against ground truth (actual tool calls).
3. **Audit completeness** is limited — hooks are blind to what the subagent actually *did*.

## Impact

Governance/adversarial-review hooks must trust the subagent's self-reported narrative (child_summary) without any way to cross-reference it against actual operations. This is a fundamental visibility gap.

## Proposed Solution

Add an optional `tool_call_history` field to the subagent_stop payload, containing a list of tool invocations made by the child agent. Each entry could include:
- `tool_name`
- `tool_input` (summary/truncated)
- `tool_output` (truncated or omitted for privacy)
- `timestamp`

This enables governance hooks to:
- Cross-reference claimed outputs in child_summary against actual file writes
- Detect undisclosed side-effects
- Compute actual operation count vs. claimed

## Current Workaround

The governance layer at `E:/work/governance/orchestrator.py` currently validates `claimed_outputs` by checking file existence on disk — but this only works for file artifacts and cannot detect operations that don't leave persistent files (network calls, variable mutations, etc.).

+        """When the supervised watcher crashes and the supervisor respawns it,
+        _reconnect_watcher_task must advance to the NEW task, not stay pinned to
+        the dead one. This is the exact condition _ensure_reconnect_watcher_running
+        checks (task.done()) before deciding to spawn a duplicate."""
+        runner = _make_runner()
+        runner._running = True
+        runner._background_tasks = set()
+        # Fast, deterministic backoff.
+        runner._MAX_SUPERVISED_RESTARTS = 5
+        runner._SUPERVISED_HEALTHY_SECS = 300
+
+        crashed_once = {"done": False}
+
+        async def _crash_then_live():
+            if not crashed_once["done"]:
+                crashed_once["done"] = True
+                raise RuntimeError("boom in outer loop")
+            await asyncio.sleep(3600)
+
+        runner._reconnect_watcher_task = None
+        first = runner._spawn_supervised(
+            _crash_then_live,
+            "platform_reconnect_watcher",
+            on_spawn=lambda t: setattr(runner, "_reconnect_watcher_task", t),
+        )
+        assert runner._reconnect_watcher_task is first
+
+        # Let the first task crash and the supervisor's backoff (2**0 = 1s here,
+        # but _attempt=0 -> min(60, 1)=1) schedule + run the respawn.
+        with patch("asyncio.sleep", new=_instant_sleep):
+            # Give the event loop turns for the _done callback + _respawn task.
+            for _ in range(20):
+                await asyncio.sleep(0)
+                if runner._reconnect_watcher_task is not first:
+                    break
+
+        # The handle must now point at the respawned (live) task, NOT the dead one.
+        assert runner._reconnect_watcher_task is not first
+        assert not runner._reconnect_watcher_task.done()
+
+        # And _ensure_reconnect_watcher_running must therefore be a no-op — it
+        # must NOT spawn a duplicate, because the tracked handle is alive.
+        spawned = []
+        original = runner._spawn_supervised
+        runner._spawn_supervised = lambda *a, **k: spawned.append(a) or original(*a, **k)
+        runner._ensure_reconnect_watcher_running()
+        assert spawned == [], "ensure spawned a duplicate watcher despite a live handle"
+
+        runner._reconnect_watcher_task.cancel()
+        try:
+            await runner._reconnect_watcher_task
+        except asyncio.CancelledError:
+            pass
+
+
+async def _instant_sleep(delay, *a, **k):
+    """asyncio.sleep replacement that yields to the loop but never waits."""
+    await _REAL_ASYNCIO_SLEEP(0)
+    return None
+
+
+_REAL_ASYNCIO_SLEEP = asyncio.sleep
problem_statement:
Gateway marks a crashed platform adapter fatal and never retries — transient upstream outage permanently kills the platform

**Version:** Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream 0ce9022e, macOS (launchd-supervised gateway).

**What happened**

The photon platform's upstream service had a transient outage (its gRPC endpoint returned UNAVAILABLE / the fronting CDN served origin-error pages). The adapter's sidecar did what it is designed to do — degraded-stream watchdog exited with code 75 so the adapter could restart it — but after repeated sidecar exits the gateway gave up permanently:

```
INFO  [photon-sidecar] photon-sidecar: upstream stream degraded for 91001ms; exiting so Hermes can restart the Photon adapter
ERROR hermes_plugins.photon_platform.adapter: [photon] sidecar exited unexpectedly (code 75) — triggering reconnect
ERROR gateway.run: Fatal photon adapter error (SIDECAR_CRASHED): Photon sidecar exited unexpectedly (code 75)
```

After the `Fatal photon adapter error` line there were no further reconnect attempts of any kind. The upstream service recovered minutes later, but the platform stayed dead inside the still-running gateway for ~17.5 hours until a manual `hermes gateway start`. The gateway itself was healthy the whole time (other platforms kept working), so nothing signaled that one platform had been silently amputated. Cron jobs with `--deliver photon` logged `delivery error: Photon standalone send failed: All connection attempts failed` on every delivery in the window.

**Expected**

A platform adapter that dies on a *transient upstream* failure should be revived: exponential-backoff retry, or a periodic revive probe (even every 10–15 minutes would have cut this outage from 17.5h to minutes), or at minimum a loud persistent signal in `gateway status` that a configured platform is in a fatal state.

**Repro sketch**

1. Run the gateway with a platform whose sidecar exits when its upstream is unreachable (photon behaves this way by design).
2. Block the upstream long enough for the crash-loop to hit the fatal threshold.
3. Unblock the upstream. The adapter never comes back; `gateway status` shows the gateway healthy.

problem_statement:
Bug: hermes update breaks stock macOS when uv entrypoint requires realpath

## Bug description

On a stock macOS installation, `hermes update` can leave the `hermes` command unusable because uv-generated venv entrypoints invoke the external `realpath` command. macOS does not ship `realpath` by default.

## Reproduction

1. Use macOS without Homebrew/coreutils and with no `realpath` on `PATH`.
2. Install Hermes through the standard git/uv installer.
3. Run `hermes update`.
4. Run `hermes` or `hermes update` again.

## Actual behavior

The generated entrypoint contains:

```sh
'''exec' "$(dirname -- "$(realpath -- "$0")")"/'python3' "$0" "$@"
```

It fails with `realpath: command not found`, then resolves the wrong Python path. A follow-up `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'` is misleading: PyYAML is present in the venv but the launcher no longer reaches that interpreter.

## Expected behavior

The standard macOS installation and `hermes update` should work without requiring Homebrew/coreutils or a system-wide `realpath` command.

## Proposed fix

Avoid the uv-generated console script in the user-facing launcher. In `scripts/install.sh` (`setup_path`), for venv installs launch the checked-in entrypoint through the venv interpreter instead:

```sh
exec "$INSTALL_DIR/venv/bin/python" "$INSTALL_DIR/hermes" "$@"
```

This preserves venv dependencies, bypasses the `realpath` dependency entirely, and is recreated correctly by every update.

## Verification

I verified the proposed command in an environment whose `PATH` excluded `realpath`; `hermes --version` completed successfully.

## Temporary workaround

A user-local `~/.local/bin/realpath` shim works, but the launcher change above avoids imposing that workaround on every macOS user.

## Environment

- macOS 12.7.6 (Intel)
- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
- uv 0.11.11

problem_statement:
[Bug]: `hermes skills update` silently replaces skills with same-named ones from a different registry (data loss)

### What happened

`hermes skills update` (no args) reported a clean success:

```
Updated 4 skill(s).
```

In reality it replaced two skills with **same-named skills from a different registry by different authors**, deleting the originals' scripts. The lockfile's `source` was silently rewritten.

| Skill | Before (`clawhub`) | After (`skills.sh`) | Damage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stock-market-pro` | 8 files incl. `scripts/{yf,news,uw,options_links,ddg_search}.py` | **1 file** (`SKILL.md`) | all 5 scripts deleted; the new `SKILL.md` still instructs `uv run --script scripts/yf price [TICKER]` → **self-referentially broken** |
| `reddit` | `scripts/reddit.mjs`, `skill-card.md`, `_meta.json`, `.clawhub/origin.json` | another author's README/SKILL.md | `reddit.mjs` deleted; the install was then blocked mid-flight by the security scanner, leaving a **half-swapped tree** |

The lockfile diff is the diagnostic fingerprint:

```diff
-  "source": "clawhub",              +  "source": "skills.sh",
-  "identifier": "stock-market-pro"  +  "identifier": "skills-sh/sundial-org/awesome-openclaw-skills/stock-market-pro"
-  "files": [8 entries]              +  "files": ["SKILL.md"]
```

### Why it's hard to notice

`hermes skills check` afterwards reports `up_to_date` — it faithfully tracks the *new* upstream. Nothing in the CLI surfaces that you're now running a different author's code. Only a file-level diff reveals it. Recovery was only cheap because `~/.hermes` happened to be a git repo.

### Root cause

Two independent defects, either of which is sufficient:

**1. `tools/skills_hub.py::check_for_skill_updates`** — the candidate-source list falls back to *every* registry when the recorded source has no adapter:

```python
candidate_sources = [src for src in sources if _source_matches(src, source_name)] or sources
```

Skill names are not namespaced across registries, so a same-named skill elsewhere satisfies `src.fetch(identifier)` and is reported as *this* entry's update.

**2. `hermes_cli/skills_hub.py::do_update`** — passes the identifier to `do_install` with no source constraint:

```python
do_install(entry["identifier"], category=category, force=True, console=c)
```

When the identifier is bare (no slash, e.g. `reddit`), `do_install` sends it through `_resolve_short_name`'s fuzzy catalog search across all sources, which picks a foreign-registry match and installs it.

`reddit` shows both interacting: the resolver picked `theglove44/reddit` from skills.sh, the security scanner then hard-blocked the install (same `export REDDIT_PASSWORD=` false positive as #59010's neighbourhood) — but **files had already been overwritten before the scan gate**, so a blocked install is not atomic.

### Expected behaviour

An update should never change a skill's source registry. A cross-registry move is a *provenance change*, not an update.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)`, macOS 26.5.2 arm64
- Affected skills sourced from `clawhub`, hijacked by `skills.sh`'s `sundial-org/awesome-openclaw-skills` mirror

### Related

Same `do_update` → `do_install(bare_name)` → `_resolve_short_name` path as the resolver problems in #6866 and #37008, but with a data-destructive outcome rather than a no-op or hang.

I have a fix + regression tests and will open a PR referencing this issue.

problem_statement:
[Bug]: `hermes update` downgrades CVE-pinned packages to stale exact versions, overwriting newer compatible installs

## Summary

Running `hermes update` downgrades actively-installed newer package versions to stale exact pins from `setup.py`, silently regressing packages that the user (or a previous update) had upgraded to newer CVE-fixing versions.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.18.0
- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (Apple Silicon)
- Python: system Python in `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have Hermes v0.18.0 installed with a venv containing newer package versions (e.g. `cryptography==48.0.1`, `starlette==1.3.1`, `python-multipart==0.0.31` — installed via manual `pip install --upgrade` or transitive resolution).
2. Run `hermes update`.
3. Observe the pip output:

```
- cryptography==48.0.1
+ cryptography==46.0.7
- python-multipart==0.0.31
+ python-multipart==0.0.27
- starlette==1.3.1
+ starlette==1.0.1
```

4. After update, the venv has the older versions installed.

## Expected Behavior

`hermes update` should not downgrade packages below their currently-installed version if the installed version also satisfies the CVE/security constraint. Exact `==` pins in `setup.py` should either:

- Be updated to the latest CVE-fixing version, **or**
- Use floor pins (`>=`) instead of exact pins (`==`) so newer compatible versions are not stripped.

## Actual Behavior

`hermes update` reinstalls from `setup.py` exact pins, downgrading:

| Package | Was | After update | Pin in setup.py | CVE reason |
|---------|------|-------------|-----------------|------------|
| cryptography | 48.0.1 | 46.0.7 | `==46.0.7` | CVE-2026-39892, CVE-2026-34073 |
| starlette | 1.3.1 | 1.0.1 | `==1.0.1` | CVE-2026-48710 (BadHost) |
| python-multipart | 0.0.31 | 0.0.27 | `==0.0.27` | (in `web` extra) |

## Root Cause

`setup.py` uses exact `==` pins for CVE-mitigated packages. These pins were correct when written, but are now stale — newer versions (48.0.1, 1.3.1, 0.0.31) also fix the same CVEs. When `hermes update` reinstalls dependencies from `setup.py`, pip's exact-pin resolution downgrades the packages.

The `cryptography==46.0.7` pin is especially aggressive: it's a transitive dependency of `PyJWT[crypto]`, and 48.0.1 is a drop-in compatible upgrade that also fixes the referenced CVEs.

## Workaround

```bash
~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/pip install --upgrade \
  cryptography==48.0.1 python-multipart==0.0.31 starlette==1.3.1
```

Must be run after **every** `hermes update`.

## Suggested Fix

1. **Update the pins** to the latest CVE-fixing versions (e.g. `cryptography==48.0.1`, `starlette==1.3.1`, `python-multipart==0.0.31`), **or**
2. **Switch to floor pins** (`cryptography>=46.0.7`, `starlette>=1.0.1`, `python-multipart>=0.0.27`) so newer compatible versions survive reinstalls, **or**
3. **Skip downgrades during update**: if the installed version satisfies the security constraint, don't force-downgrade.

## Related

- #53272 — `hermes update` does not reinstall active memory provider pip dependencies
- #59026 — Langfuse SDK silently removed from venv after update
- #39424 — stale `hindsight-client==0.6.1` pin

problem_statement:
fix(lazy-deps): active_features() presence-only check causes false-positive activation and unnecessary downgrades

### Problem

`tools/lazy_deps.py:538-552` - active_features() uses _is_present() which checks only if a package name exists at any version.

If aiohttp 3.14.1 is installed by any dependency, platform.slack is reported as active because its spec aiohttp==3.13.4 matches on package name. Then refresh_active_features() triggers pip install aiohttp==3.13.4 - a downgrade.

### Impact

- Unnecessary pip operations during hermes update
- Potential downgrade from working to older pinned version
- On Windows, downgrade can fail if gateway holds .pyd files open

### Suggested Fix

Option A: Use _is_satisfied() instead of _is_present() in active_features().
Option B: Only match on the feature's primary package (first spec).

problem_statement:
save_env_value writes unquoted values with internal spaces - breaks shell-sourcing of .env (core-writer sibling of #57247)

## Impact (first)

Real flows write **filesystem paths that routinely contain spaces** into `~/.hermes/.env` via the core writer `save_env_value` → `_quote_env_value`:

| Flow | Env key | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| `hermes setup` → SSH backend | `TERMINAL_SSH_KEY` | `hermes_cli/setup.py` (~1416) `save_env_value("TERMINAL_SSH_KEY", ssh_key)` |
| Google Chat setup | `GOOGLE_CHAT_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` | `plugins/platforms/google_chat/adapter.py` (~3484) |
| `hermes config set TERMINAL_SSH_KEY …` / `terminal.ssh_key` | same / via terminal env bridge | `set_config_value` → `save_env_value` (`hermes_cli/config.py`) |

**macOS is most exposed**: paths under `~/Library/Application Support/...` are common for keys and service-account JSON. Windows `Program Files` / user profile spaces are also in-scope when those paths are saved through the same writer.

## Repro (upstream/main @ `bcea5371c`)

Throwaway `HERMES_HOME`, real `save_env_value`:

```text
value = /Users/paulo/Library/Application Support/hermes/keys/id_ed25519
```

**Emitted line (verbatim):**
```text
TERMINAL_SSH_KEY=/Users/paulo/Library/Application Support/hermes/keys/id_ed25519
```

**python-dotenv:** OK — returns the full path (masks the bug for Hermes runtime load).

**Shell source:**
```bash
env -i sh -c 'set -a; . file; set +a'
```
**Exact error:**
```text
.env: line 1: Support/hermes/keys/id_ed25519: No such file or directory
```
(`TERMINAL_SSH_KEY` ends up empty / truncated after word-split.)

## Trigger condition (line numbers on this base)

`hermes_cli/config.py` `_quote_env_value` @ **7772**, used by `save_env_value` @ **7788**:

```python
needs_quoting = (
    "#" in value
    or '"' in value
    or "'" in value
    or value != value.strip()
)
```

Internal whitespace (space/tab between non-space characters) does **not** trigger quoting. Only `#`, quotes, or leading/trailing whitespace do.

## Why python-dotenv masks it

`python-dotenv` / `dotenv_values` treat unquoted values as running to EOL (modulo `#` comments). Shell `.` / `source` with `set -a` does POSIX word-splitting on unquoted assignment RHS / bare path fragments after the first space — so tools that shell-source `.env` (debug scripts, containers, `set -a; . ~/.hermes/.env`) break while Hermes itself keeps working.

## Class link (honest)

| Item | Surface | Status |
|------|---------|--------|
| **#57247** (accepted) | Installer writer for `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` | Bug accepted |
| **#57249** | Fixes **only** the installer (`install.sh` / `install.ps1`) | Does **not** touch `hermes_cli/config.py` |
| **#57449** | Competing installer-only PR | Same installer surface; **not** core serializer |
| **This issue** | **Core serializer** `_quote_env_value` / `save_env_value` | Sibling class: same unquoted-spaced-path failure mode, different write path |

#57249 is the right dialect (`\\` then `\"` then wrap) already used by `_quote_env_value`; the gap is the **trigger** missing internal whitespace, not the escape algorithm.

## Platform statement

- **Reproduced** on macOS with a real spaced path under Application Support.
- Failure mode is **POSIX shell sourcing**, not Hermes' primary dotenv load path.
- Fix is portable: quote when `any(c.isspace() for c in value)`; no install-script changes (those remain #57249's surface).

## Expected fix

Extend `needs_quoting` only (escaping/wrapping **unchanged**). Idempotent re-save; no mass-requote of unrelated `.env` keys on next write of a different key.

A UTF-16 .env silently corrupts the first key - and the sanitizer writes the corruption back to disk

## Impact

Saving `~/.hermes/.env` as **Unicode (UTF-16 LE + BOM)** from Windows Notepad (or any editor that writes UTF-16) causes Hermes to **silently drop the first env key** and then **permanently rewrite the on-disk file in a mangled form**.

- No error is raised.
- Canonical `os.environ.get("HERMES_TEST_KEY")` returns `None`.
- The first key appears under a mangled name like `\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY`.
- On the next startup, the sanitizer has already rewritten the file with U+FFFD bytes baked in (`EF BF BD EF BF BD...`), so the corruption **survives** even if the user later opens the file in a UTF-8 editor.

This is worse than a pure load bug: the pre-load sanitizer **persists** the damage.

## Byte-level repro (macOS / Linux; emulates Notepad "Unicode")

Against current `main` (`bcea5371c`):

```python
import codecs, os, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from hermes_cli.env_loader import load_hermes_dotenv

home = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
env = home / ".env"
content = "HERMES_TEST_KEY=hello_utf16\nSECOND_KEY=world\n"
env.write_bytes(codecs.BOM_UTF16_LE + content.encode("utf-16-le"))

os.environ.pop("HERMES_TEST_KEY", None)
os.environ.pop("SECOND_KEY", None)
load_hermes_dotenv(hermes_home=home)

print("canonical:", repr(os.environ.get("HERMES_TEST_KEY")))
print("mangled  :", repr(os.environ.get("\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY")))
print("on disk  :", env.read_bytes()[:40].hex())
```

### Observed before fix

| Encoding | Canonical first key | Mangled key | On-disk after load |
|----------|---------------------|-------------|--------------------|
| UTF-16-LE + BOM | `None` | `\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY=hello_utf16` | rewritten: starts `ef bf bd ef bf bd...` |
| UTF-16-BE + BOM | `None` | same class of mangling | rewritten mangled |
| UTF-16-LE no BOM | loads (accidental) | n/a | often repaired via NUL strip |
| UTF-16-BE no BOM | loads (accidental) | n/a | often repaired via NUL strip |

Mangled key name (LE+BOM, after rewrite) is literally U+FFFD U+FFFD glued to the original key: `\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY` with value `hello_utf16`.

## Mechanism

`_sanitize_env_file_if_needed` (was lines ~167-217 on `main`) does:

1. `open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig", errors="replace")`
2. For a UTF-16 BOM (`FF FE` / `FE FF`), those two bytes are not a UTF-8 BOM, so they become **two U+FFFD replacement characters** glued to the first key name.
3. Embedded NUL bytes (the other half of every UTF-16 code unit for ASCII) are stripped.
4. Because `sanitized != original`, the result is written back with `mkstemp` + `fsync` + `atomic_replace` as UTF-8, **permanently** storing the U+FFFD-prefixed key.

BOM-less UTF-16 of pure ASCII happens to look like NUL-padded ASCII; the existing NUL strip path accidentally "repairs" it. That is coincidence, not a design.

## Relationship to #65123 / #65124

**Sibling, not duplicate.**

| | #65123 / #65124 | This issue |
|--|-----------------|------------|
| Encoding | UTF-8 + BOM (`EF BB BF`) | UTF-16 + BOM (`FF FE` / `FE FF`) |
| Root cause | `load_dotenv(encoding="utf-8")` keeps U+FEFF on the first key | **Sanitizer** decode with `errors=replace` then **rewrite** |
| Disk mutation | No (load-time only) | **Yes** - file permanently mangled |
| Fix surface | `_load_dotenv_with_fallback` (+ send_cmd) | `_sanitize_env_file_if_needed` |

#65248 is UTF-8 BOM only in sanitize (related but not UTF-16).

Cross-link: #65123

## Environment

- Python: 3.11 (venv `python3.11`)
- hermes-agent: 0.18.2 (`pyproject.toml`)
- python-dotenv: 1.2.2
- OS: macOS (Darwin arm64)

## Platform honesty

Repro is **byte-level emulation** of Notepad "Unicode" / UTF-16-LE+BOM and UTF-16-BE+BOM (and BOM-less variants). PowerShell 5.1 and Notepad were **not** executed on a Windows host in this run.

## Expected behavior

- UTF-16 (with BOM) `.env` should load the first key under its **canonical** name.
- On-disk file should be rewritten as **clean UTF-8** (no BOM, no U+FFFD), or left untouched if the encoding is unsupported (e.g. UTF-32: refuse-to-mangle).
- Never persist `errors=replace` garbage back to disk.

[Bug]%20_resolve_task_provider_model%20ignores%20key_env%20field%20in%20auxiliary%20task%20config%20%E2%86%92%20vision/compression%20401

## Summary

`_resolve_task_provider_model()` in `agent/auxiliary_client.py` reads `api_key` from the auxiliary task config but **never reads `key_env`** (or `api_key_env`). When a user configures an auxiliary task with `key_env` instead of a plaintext `api_key`, the resolved API key is `None`, and requests are sent with the `"no-key-required"` placeholder → `401 AuthenticationError` on every call.

## Reproduction

```yaml
# ~/.hermes/config.yaml
auxiliary:
  vision:
    provider: custom
    model: qwen3.7-plus
    base_url: https://coding.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1
    key_env: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY      # ← this field is NEVER parsed
    timeout: 120
```

```bash
# .env has the key
DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=sk-sp-xxxxxxxxxxxx
```

```python
# vision_analyze tool fails every time:
# openai.AuthenticationError: Error code: 401 - {'error': {'code': 'invalid_api_key', ...}}
```

## Root Cause

`agent/auxiliary_client.py`, function `_resolve_task_provider_model()` (line ~5888):

```python
cfg_api_key = str(task_config.get("api_key", "")).strip() or None
# ← key_env is never consulted here
cfg_api_mode = str(task_config.get("api_mode", "")).strip() or None
```

The `key_env` field **is** correctly parsed in two other places in the same file:
- `_fallback_entry_api_key()` (L3987) — reads `key_env`/`api_key_env`
- named custom provider resolution (L4721) — reads `key_env`/`api_key_env`

But the top-level auxiliary task config resolution path in `_resolve_task_provider_model()` does not.

## Impact

Any auxiliary task (`vision`, `compression`, `web_extract`, `session_search`) configured with `key_env` instead of inline `api_key` will fail with 401. This is the documented/recommended way to configure credentials (keeping secrets in `.env`, not `config.yaml`), so users following best practices hit this bug.

Related issues:
- #9318 — similar symptom (no-key-required fallback) but different root cause (wants to inherit `model.api_key`)
- #16254 — mentions `key_env never parsed in aux config` as a side note

## Fix

Add `key_env` resolution in `_resolve_task_provider_model()` right after reading `cfg_api_key`:

```python
cfg_api_key = str(task_config.get("api_key", "")).strip() or None
# Resolve key_env → env var if api_key is not set directly
if not cfg_api_key:
    cfg_key_env = str(task_config.get("key_env") or task_config.get("api_key_env") or "").strip()
    if cfg_key_env:
        cfg_api_key = os.getenv(cfg_key_env, "").strip() or None
cfg_api_mode = str(task_config.get("api_mode", "")).strip() or None
```

This mirrors the same `key_env`/`api_key_env` fallback pattern already used in `_fallback_entry_api_key()` and named custom provider resolution.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 15.5 (Apple Silicon M4 Max)
- Config: `auxiliary.vision.provider: custom` with `key_env: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`

[Bug]: System prompt hardcodes ~/.hermes, misdirecting the agent under a non-default HERMES_HOME

## Bug Description

`agent/system_prompt.py` (`build_system_prompt_parts`) describes the agent's own filesystem layout using hardcoded `~/.hermes/...` literals rather than deriving it from `get_hermes_home()`. Under any non-default `HERMES_HOME` — the Docker default `/opt/data`, or profile mode where `HERMES_HOME` is `<root>/profiles/<name>` — the system prompt states paths that **do not exist**, and the agent believes them.

This is not cosmetic: the agent acts on the prompt. Ours repeatedly issued `search_files` against the non-existent path, failed with `Path not found`, and burned iterations (in some rounds exhausting its iteration budget without answering).

Notably, `hermes_constants.get_hermes_home()` already documents itself as the fix:
> Reads HERMES_HOME env var, falls back to `~/.hermes`. **This is the single source of truth — all other copies should import this.**

The tools (`browser_tool.py`, `browser_camofox*.py`, …) and the cross-profile guard (`agent/file_safety.py`) already import it. `agent/system_prompt.py` is the outlier that hardcodes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the gateway with a non-default home, e.g. Docker `-e HERMES_HOME=/opt/data`.
2. Activate a named profile — `hermes_cli/profiles.py:1106` sets `os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = str(profile_dir)`, so `get_hermes_home()` → `/opt/data/profiles/coder`.
3. Ask the agent to look at its own skills / memories / plugins.
4. The prompt tells it to read `~/.hermes/profiles/coder/`, which resolves to a path that does not exist; the agent issues failing `search_files` calls.

## Expected Behavior

The system prompt names the agent's real directories, derived from `get_hermes_home()` / `get_default_hermes_root()`, so the agent looks in the right place.

## Actual Behavior

The prompt hardcodes `~/.hermes/...`. In our container (`HERMES_HOME=/opt/data`, profile mode):

```
EXISTS   /opt/data/profiles/coder          <- the real profile dir (== get_hermes_home())
MISSING  /opt/data/.hermes/profiles/coder  <- where the prompt sends the agent
MISSING  /root/.hermes                      <- literal ~/.hermes
```

The failure is independent of how `~` expands — neither `/root/.hermes` nor `/opt/data/.hermes` exists. The only correct value is `get_hermes_home()`.

## Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory) — specifically system-prompt assembly. Platform-agnostic (affects every profile/adapter, not a specific messaging platform).

## Debug Report

Not attached deliberately: this is a code-level defect fully determined by `agent/system_prompt.py` + the value of `HERMES_HOME`, reproducible from source without runtime state, and we would rather not upload a self-hosted deployment's config/logs to a public paste. Everything needed to reproduce is above. Happy to provide more on request.

## Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) container, on Ubuntu 24.04 host.

## Python Version

3.13.5

## Hermes Version

0.15.1

## Additional Logs / Traceback

```
Tool search_files returned error: {"total_count": 0,
  "error": "Path not found: /opt/data/.hermes/profiles/coder"}
Tool search_files returned error: {"total_count": 0,
  "error": "Path not found: /opt/data/.hermes/profiles/coder/skills"}
```

## Root Cause Analysis

`agent/system_prompt.py` hardcodes the default layout in four places inside `build_system_prompt_parts`:

- **L250** (default branch): `"...Other profiles (if any) live under ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/..."`
- **L259** (named-profile branch): `f"...This session reads and writes ~/.hermes/profiles/{active_profile}/..."`
- **L260–261**: `f"...The default profile's data lives at ~/.hermes/skills/, ~/.hermes/plugins/, ~/.hermes/cron/, ~/.hermes/memories/..."`

The module does not import `hermes_constants`, so it has no way to know the real home.

Two knock-on effects worth noting:
- The **cross-profile isolation guidance** lives in this same string. The prompt tells the agent not to touch other profiles' `skills/plugins/cron/memories` and names them by path — under a non-default home those paths are wrong, so the safety instruction points at locations that don't exist while the real ones go unnamed. (The *enforcement* in `agent/file_safety.py` is unaffected — it resolves real paths — so this is a "the agent is misinformed" bug, not a data-safety bug.)

## Proposed Fix

Derive the paths from the existing helpers, matching `agent/file_safety.py`. Both helpers already exist in `hermes_constants`:
- `get_hermes_home()` → this session's own dir (the profile dir in profile mode)
- `get_default_hermes_root()` → the profiles root / default-profile data

```diff
     TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS,
 )
+from hermes_constants import get_default_hermes_root, get_hermes_home

@@ default-profile branch
         stable_parts.append(
             "Active Hermes profile: default. Other profiles (if any) live "
-            "under ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/. Each profile has its own "
+            f"under {get_default_hermes_root()}/profiles/<name>/. Each profile has its own "
             ...

@@ named-profile branch
     else:
+        _root = get_default_hermes_root()
         stable_parts.append(
             f"Active Hermes profile: {active_profile}. This session reads "
-            f"and writes ~/.hermes/profiles/{active_profile}/. The default "
-            f"profile's data lives at ~/.hermes/skills/, ~/.hermes/plugins/, "
-            f"~/.hermes/cron/, ~/.hermes/memories/ — those belong to a "
+            f"and writes {get_hermes_home()}/. The default "
+            f"profile's data lives at {_root}/skills/, {_root}/plugins/, "
+            f"{_root}/cron/, {_root}/memories/ — those belong to a "
             ...
```

Verified against 0.15.1: applies, compiles, and renders correct paths (e.g. `writes /opt/data/profiles/coder/`).

+++ b/apps/desktop/electron/backend-health.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
+export const DEFAULT_BACKEND_READY_TIMEOUT_MS = 45_000
+export const DEFAULT_BACKEND_READY_POLL_MS = 500
+// A cold backend can stall its event loop for tens of seconds while Windows
+// scans and byte-compiles the gateway import tree. At the default 15s socket
+// timeout only three probes fit in the budget; a short one keeps retrying
+// across the stall. Health only — the legacy /api/status fallback is genuinely
+// slow to answer and keeps the caller's default timeout.
+export const DEFAULT_HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000
+
+type FetchPublicJson = (url: string, options?: { timeoutMs?: number }) => Promise<unknown>
+type FetchJson = (url: string, token?: string | null, options?: { timeoutMs?: number }) => Promise<unknown>
+
+export interface HermesReadyOptions {
+  fetchPublicJson: FetchPublicJson
+  fetchJson: FetchJson
+  token?: string | null
+  signal?: AbortSignal
+  timeoutMs?: number
+  pollMs?: number
+  healthProbeTimeoutMs?: number
+  sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>
+  now?: () => number
+}
+
+export function isMissingHealthEndpointError(error: unknown): boolean {
+  const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error ?? '')
+
+  return /^404:/.test(message) || message.includes('endpoint is likely missing')
+}
+
+function supersededError() {
+  const error: any = new Error('SSH bootstrap was superseded by newer connection settings.')
+  error.kind = 'superseded'
+
+  return error
+}
+
+export async function waitForHermesReady(baseUrl: string, options: HermesReadyOptions): Promise<void> {
+  const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_BACKEND_READY_TIMEOUT_MS
+  const pollMs = options.pollMs ?? DEFAULT_BACKEND_READY_POLL_MS
+  const healthProbeTimeoutMs = options.healthProbeTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS
+  const now = options.now ?? Date.now
+  const signal = options.signal
+
+  const sleep =
+    options.sleep ??
+    (ms =>
+      new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
+        const timer = setTimeout(resolve, ms)
+        signal?.addEventListener(
+          'abort',
+          () => {
+            clearTimeout(timer)
+            reject(supersededError())
+          },
+          { once: true }
+        )
+      }))
+
+  const base = baseUrl.replace(/\/+$/, '')
+  const deadline = now() + timeoutMs
+  let lastError: unknown = null
+  let useStatusFallback = false
+
+  while (now() < deadline) {
+    if (signal?.aborted) {
+      throw supersededError()
+    }
+
+    try {
+      if (useStatusFallback) {
+        await options.fetchJson(`${base}/api/status`, options.token)
+      } else {
+        await options.fetchPublicJson(`${base}/api/health`, { timeoutMs: healthProbeTimeoutMs })
+      }
+
+      return
+    } catch (error) {
+      lastError = error
+
+      // Only an explicitly missing route means the backend predates
+      // /api/health; timeouts and server errors keep polling health.
+      if (!useStatusFallback && isMissingHealthEndpointError(error)) {
+        useStatusFallback = true
+
+        continue
+      }
+
+      await sleep(pollMs)
+    }
+  }
+
+  const detail = lastError instanceof Error ? lastError.message : 'timeout'
+  throw new Error(`Hermes backend did not become ready: ${detail}`)
+}

problem_statement: [comp/desktop] Desktop boot fails when platform adapter import or MCP registration exceeds the 15s readiness timeout ### Environment - Hermes Agent version: v0.18.0 (commit 5eac6652, Electron build win-unpacked) - OS: Windows 10 (native install, not WSL) - Default install: 7 MCP servers + 21 bundled platform adapters - Hermes CLI / Dashboard: work normally - Hermes Desktop: boot fails on every launch ### Summary Hermes Desktop on Windows fails to start with "Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms". The backend reports HERMES_BACKEND_READY within ~5s and /api/health responds in <100 ms, but the Electron readiness probe waits for /api/status, which blocks for the full 15s window and then triggers the error dialog. The boot loop retries 4 times before giving up. ### Root cause The 15 s budget is spent entirely inside /api/status -> load_gateway_config() -> platform_registry._resolve_all(), which eagerly imports every deferred platform adapter. On the default install with 21 platforms, this takes 12-13 s on first call. Adding register_mcp_servers() on top makes the first-request budget roughly 24 s. The CLI and Dashboard never hit /api/status at startup, so they are unaffected. Measured on this machine (cProfile + stopwatch): - register_mcp_servers(7 servers): 23.91 s first call - load_gateway_config(): 12.83 s first call - platform_registry.plugin_entries() (21 plugins): 12.36 s of that 12.83 s - yaml.safe_load(config.yaml, 18 KB): 0.09 s - discover_plugins(): 1.05 s After deleting 19 of 21 platform plugin folders (keeping only telegram/) /api/status responds in 3 s and Desktop starts cleanly. There is no config knob to achieve the same effect without deleting files. ### Suggested fixes (any one would unblock the user) 1. Make the Desktop timeout configurable. apps/desktop/electron/hardening.cjs hardcodes DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000. Read it from env HERMES_DESKTOP_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS or from config.yaml under desktop.fetch_timeout_ms. Smallest change, pure escape hatch. 2. Honor plugins.disabled / platforms..enabled: false in the cold-start path. gateway/config.py:_apply_env_overrides() and platform_registry._resolve_all() need to consult _get_disabled_plugins() (already correctly read in hermes_cli/plugins.py:180) before importing each deferred adapter. The Slack fix from commit 156176a44 (the _enable_from_env helper plus _enabled_explicit marker) is the pattern -- it just has not been migrated to Discord, Telegram, etc. Without this, even users who explicitly disable a platform in config.yaml still pay its 0.5-2 s import cost. 3. Defer cold-start work past the readiness probe. /api/status should return "process is up, uvicorn is listening" in <1 s. The heavy register_mcp_servers + load_gateway_config should run in a background coroutine after HERMES_BACKEND_READY is emitted; the renderer polls a separate /api/tools/ready endpoint. This is the only fix that scales -- users with 10 MCP servers and 5 enabled platforms will eventually hit the timeout even with #1 and #2 in place. A useful intermediate for #3: there is already _warm_gateway_module() in hermes_cli/web_server.py:157 running in run_in_executor. # OpenRouter requests don't send `session_id` → no sticky routing / prompt caching for paid multi-turn
## Summary
Hermes does not forward `session_id` to OpenRouter on chat requests. This disables OpenRouter's sticky-routing + prompt-caching for multi-turn agent loops.
## Evidence
- Searched `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/agent/auxiliary_client.py` for `session_id|extra_body|session|sticky` → 0 matches.
- `tools/openrouter_client.py` only builds the client via the centralized router; no `extra_body` injection.
- Hermes does per-conversation prefix caching internally (per AGENTS.md), but that's a separate layer from OpenRouter's API-level `session_id`.
## Impact
For paid OpenRouter models (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` via OpenRouter), multi-turn agent loops hit a *cold* provider on turn 2 → full input price, no cache reuse. The OpenRouter blog recommends `session_id` to pin the session to the provider holding the warm cache from turn 1. Free `:free` tier is unaffected (volatile routing).
## Proposed fix (~5 lines)
In the OpenRouter request path, inject a stable-per-conversation id:
```python
extra_body = {"session_id": <stable conversation_id>}
```
where `conversation_id` is already available internally and stable for the life of the conversation.
## Docs reference
https://openrouter.ai/blog/tutorials/prompt-caching-sticky-routing/
## Environment
- Hermes Agent (Nous Research), macOS
- Provider: OpenRouter (paid models used sporadically; `:free` daily)
- Repro: any multi-turn conversation using a paid OpenRouter model → check `cached_tokens` in usage response → stays 0 / low across turns because requests land on different provider endpoints (no sticky routing).

problem_statement:
Docker image ships WAL-reset-vulnerable SQLite (Debian trixie libsqlite3 3.46.1) — no fixed-SQLite path for image installs (parity with #70200/#70186)

The official image (`FROM debian:13.4`, apt `python3`, venv via `uv sync` on the system interpreter) dynamically links `libsqlite3-0 3.46.1-7+deb13u1`, which `hermes doctor` itself flags as vulnerable to the WAL-reset corruption bug (https://sqlite.org/wal.html#walresetbug, fixed 3.51.3+, backports 3.50.7 / 3.44.6). Debian trixie carries no backport (its latest changelog entry, 2026-01-22, only addresses CVE-2025-7709), so `docker pull` + recreate keeps shipping the vulnerable library indefinitely.

#70200 / #70186 repair managed (uv / python-build-standalone) installs, but image installs have no equivalent path; the #70055 DELETE-mode gate protects only NEW shared DBs, so pre-existing WAL databases (`kanban.db`, `state.db`) on busy multi-worker boards still ride the vulnerable checkpoint path — we have observed live `kanban.db` corruption fences on 0.19.0 under concurrent-worker load.

**Request:** bake a fixed SQLite (>= 3.51.3; #70200 targets 3.53.1) into the published image — e.g. compile the pinned autoconf amalgamation into `/usr/local/lib/<multiarch>` ahead of the distro lib, or install a fixed `libsqlite3-0` — and/or document an endorsed override for derived images.

Happy to share our derived-image layer (pinned 3.53.3 build with SHA3 verification and build-time version/FTS5 asserts) as a reference.

problem_statement:
Variables injected in doctest_namespace no longer loaded in Pytest 9.1.x

### Description

I'm running into issues with `pytest` 9.1.x when running my doctests. I've been able to inject variables and functions into the namespace for doctests via a fixture so that I don't need to explicitly write these things into all my doctests, e.g.:
```python
@pytest.fixture(scope="session", autouse=True)
def doctest_setup(doctest_namespace, nimbus, worker_id, open_dataset) -> None:  # numpydoc ignore=PR01
    """Gather testing data on doctest run."""
    testing_setup_warnings()
    gather_testing_data(worker_cache_dir=nimbus.path, worker_id=worker_id)
    doctest_namespace.update(custom_testing_data(nimbus=nimbus))

    class AttrDict(dict):  # numpydoc ignore=PR01
        """A dictionary that allows access to its keys as attributes."""

        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
            super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
            self.__dict__ = self

    xr = AttrDict()
    xr["DataArray"] = xarray.DataArray
    xr["date_range"] = xarray.date_range
    xr["open_dataset"] = custom_library.open_dataset
    doctest_namespace["xr"] = xr

    doctest_namespace.update(add_doctest_filepaths())
    doctest_namespace.update(add_example_file_paths())
```

This has been working well for many years, but it seems like there's been a major change in how the latest `pytest` collects/runs fixtures for doctests.

All my tests are now failing with `NameError: name '<variable/function name injected from doctest_setup>' is not defined`.
